solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Start to concentrate before bishop leads meeting in intellectual manner

indicators.note: whatever leads goes in front, so the bishop's letter heads the meeting word

parts.note: a rally is a mass meeting

explanation.surface: Advice to a thinker: focus first, then let the bishop chair the meeting in a suitably brainy way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' is not a positional instruction but a word in its own right, the old poetic synonym; only 'leads' does any placing.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerebral means of the intellect, so cerebrally is doing something in an intellectual manner.

clue.text: Composer using four notes — or none!

definitions.text: Composer using four notes — or none!

parts.words: Composer using four notes — or none!
parts.note: the composer's name is spelt with four letters that are all musical notes, and his most famous piece has the performers play no notes at all

explanation.walkthrough: The 'or none!' joke refers to John Cage's 4'33", a piece in which the performers play nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: John Cage was an American avant-garde composer, famous for his silent piece.

clue.text: Money that is held by opposing sides

parts.note: right and left, opposite sides; splits as R...L

explanation.surface: Cash that is clutched between two sides in a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opposing sides' sounds like two teams or parties; it is just right and left.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Cambodia's currency unit, divided into 100 sen.

clue.text: French mathematician developed basis with Laplace

indicators.note: the letters are worked up into a new form

explanation.surface: A French mathematician built his theory on foundations laid alongside Laplace.
explanation.walkthrough: Laplace, himself a French mathematician, is a decoy for the answer and merely supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Blaise Pascal, 17th-century French mathematician of Pascal's triangle.

clue.text: Fine instrument used in dramatisation

indicators.note: the answer is found in use inside the next word

parts.note: the answer sits in letters three to seven of this word

explanation.surface: A fine instrument features in a stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: An Amati is a violin made by the Amati family of Cremona, forerunners of Stradivari.
explanation.definitionFit: Amati violins are prized instruments, so 'fine' is fair.

clue.text: Story about female underwear I start to read in bookshop abroad

indicators.note: about means around, so the story wraps the other pieces

parts.note: a story can be a lie, an untruth
a bra is a woman's undergarment

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of each of the words read and in

explanation.surface: Someone browsing in a foreign bookshop reads a racy story about lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog found the clue faulty, and the editor changed 'start to' to 'originally'; read as the first letters of 'read in', it still works.
explanation.definitionFit: Librairie is the French word for a bookshop, so it is a bookshop found overseas.

clue.text: Bird lives on Irish beaches primarily

indicators.note: on means placed after, so lives follows the two initials
primarily means first, so the opening letters of Irish and beaches are taken

parts.note: lives means exists, which is is

explanation.surface: A bird that makes its home along the beaches of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a long, down-curved bill.

clue.text: For instance, net something no longer deemed fashionable?

definitions.meaning: net written backwards spells a number word
a person or thing that is out of date, like an old magazine issue

explanation.surface: A fishing net, say, is something that has gone out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic riddle: NET is TEN written back to front, so it is literally a number backwards, a 'back number'.
explanation.definitionFit: A back number is an old issue of a periodical, hence anyone or anything out of date.

clue.text: Parable I utilised in original way to convey meaning primarily

indicators.note: to convey means to carry, so the rearranged letters hold the extra letter
used in an original way means reworked creatively, so the letters of I utilised are rearranged
primarily means the first letter of meaning

explanation.surface: A writer explains that they used a parable in an inventive way to put their meaning across.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of I UTILISED is SIIILTUDE in some order; the M goes in after SI to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A similitude is an old word for a comparison or allegory, such as a parable that explains by likeness.

clue.text: Actress to feel bad about taking off a dress — nothing to finish with!

indicators.note: the zero comes at the finish, as the last piece of the answer

parts.note: to regret something is to feel bad about it

explanation.surface: An actress regretting that she took off a dress and has nothing left to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feel bad about' reads as one phrase, but 'about' is split off to be removed, the usual 'concerning' abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was the Swedish-born Hollywood star.

clue.text: Trick rogue, quietly departing

indicators.note: departing means leaving, so the letter walks out of the word

parts.note: P = piano, quietly in music; removed

explanation.surface: A rogue slipping away silently after pulling a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: P for piano is the musical marking for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a scam is a con, a dishonest trick for money.

clue.text: Legislation brought by British, bad old folk not looking good

parts.note: a fright is an unsightly person, as in 'you look a fright'

explanation.surface: A law passed by the British against wicked, unattractive old people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad old folk' looks like one unit, but it breaks into ILL, O and the FRIGHTS who are not looking good.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bill of Rights is the 1689 English statute, and the US amendments, both legislation.

clue.text: A small number helping almost everyone having high hopes

parts.note: a helping is a portion, a ration

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its last letter

explanation.surface: Only a few people help, and almost everyone is full of high hopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small number' wants to be one idea, but it splits: S for small, PI for the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirational describes someone keen to get on in life, full of ambition.

clue.text: At rest, so we abandoned cars

indicators.note: the letters are thrown about with abandon

explanation.surface: Parked and still, the cars had been left behind by their owners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned cars' is such a natural phrase that 'abandoned' hides its job; here it means wild, without restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-seaters are small cars with room for only two.

clue.text: Change still perceived as feature of church

indicators.note: to be perceived is to be taken in by the senses, here by the listening ear

explanation.surface: A sign that change is still regarded as part of church life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' is a noun here, as in 'the still of the night', giving PEACE rather than 'yet'.
explanation.definitionFit: An altarpiece is the painting or carving behind a church altar.

clue.text: Poet Edmund eats soft food that comes in rolls

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a noun: something that comes in rolls

parts.note: Edmund Waller, 17th-century English poet; splits as WALL...ER

explanation.surface: A poet eating mush, with 'food that comes in rolls' suggesting bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Food that comes in rolls' looks like bread; the definition is only 'that comes in rolls', and the food is the PAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the decorator's paper is sold wound on rolls, which is what the clue points to.

clue.text: Right to graze cattle in former city once upon a time

indicators.note: 'in' puts one thing inside another, so the city sits within the phrase for olden days

parts.note: a past age, splits as PAST...AGE

explanation.surface: An ancient grazing right from a long-vanished city.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur of the Chaldees is the crossword's favourite ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasturage is pasture land and, in law, the right to graze animals on it.

clue.text: Restrict learner with self-aggrandizing boast

parts.note: 'I'm it', claiming to be the top person

explanation.surface: Rein in the learner driver who keeps bragging.
explanation.walkthrough: I'M IT is the boast of someone who thinks they are the best.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to limit something is to keep it within set bounds, to restrict it.

clue.text: Examinations of small vessel within bigger one

indicators.note: within means inside, so the small vessel is placed inside the bigger one's letters

parts.note: SS = steamship, a bigger vessel; splits as S...S
a can is a small container

explanation.surface: Inspections of a small boat carried aboard a larger ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' is a ship on the surface but a container for CAN, while the bigger vessel really is a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a scan is a close look, whether by a radiographer or an eye running over a page.

clue.text: City halved effort to stop protection

indicators.note: only the first half of 'effort' is used

parts.note: a shield is protection; splits as SH...IELD

explanation.surface: A city's defences weakened because its protection effort was cut in half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Halved' belongs to 'effort', not to 'City'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the South Yorkshire city famous for steel and cutlery.

clue.text: Human replica evolved like characters in Fahrenheit 451?

indicators.note: the letters change into a new form

explanation.surface: A science-fiction scenario of an evolving android in Ray Bradbury's dystopia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters in Fahrenheit 451' suggests the people in Bradbury's novel; it means the printed characters of the title, letters and digits.
explanation.definitionFit: The title mixes letters and numbers, which is what alphanumeric means.

clue.text: One apprehended by journalist with court order

parts.note: CT = court, as in street names

explanation.surface: Someone arrested by a reporter who carries a court order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court order' looks like the definition, but 'court' is CT and only 'order' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a decree issued by a ruler or authority is a command, an order.

clue.text: Particle of meat, not dry

indicators.note: 'not dry' asks for the meat without its dry element, so those letters are simply dropped

explanation.surface: A scrap of meat that has not been dried.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is teetotal: a dry person drinks no alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: The muon is a subatomic particle, a heavy cousin of the electron.

clue.text: Party's set up something to eat

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means written upwards

parts.note: the DUP, Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party, plus 's

explanation.surface: A political party has laid on some food.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party, and the 's joins it.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the informal word means a potato, which is certainly something to eat.

clue.text: English lord failing to keep right sword

explanation.surface: An English nobleman losing his grip on his rightful sword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing to keep' drops a letter rather than a possession.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one of the three weapons of modern fencing, the heaviest, is a sword.

clue.text: Foreign capital quietly blocking raised matter of only local interest

parts.note: a hump is a raised mass; splits as H...UMP

explanation.surface: Something in a far-off capital is obstructing a matter that only concerns locals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised matter' sounds like an issue brought up; it is a physical lump, a HUMP.
explanation.definitionFit: Parish-pump politics are petty and parochial, like gossip round the village pump.

clue.text: Killed a large number

definitions.meaning: an informal noun, originally American, for a great many

explanation.surface: Many people were killed.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase, it sounds like a massacre; it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Slew is the past tense of slay, and also an informal word for a great many.

clue.text: Ditched plane caught side on in crash

indicators.note: the letters are smashed up
caught by the ear, as in 'I caught what you said'

parts.note: jet = plane; JETT is said the same way

explanation.surface: A plane hit side-on in a crash had to be ditched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditched plane' reads as an aircraft landing on water, but 'Ditched' alone defines. The extra T is justified only by sound, JETT being heard as JET.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw overboard or ditch.
